title: Wishlist
summary: Everyone has a wishlist. Family members can reserve a gift or buy it together, without spoiling the surprise.

blocks.text: At the top of the Wishlist page there is a row of buttons, one for each person. Choose a person to open their list. Your own button says (You). Everyone with access to the Wishlist can see every list. Under the person buttons, a second row called **Group lists** holds the lists that belong to several people (see [Group lists](#group-lists)).

sections.title: Adding a wish to your list

blocks.title: Where to click
items: Open your own list.
Press **Add wish**.
Type a title. Everything else is optional.
Press **Save wish**.

**Links**: up to 5 addresses of shops or pages, each with an optional label. When you paste the first link into a new wish, an empty **Title** and **Notes** are filled in from that page and the picture is shown. The picture is attached when you save. Text you typed yourself is never overwritten, and you can change anything. Later links are not read. If something could not be loaded, a message names it (image, title or description) and, when known, why. If a shop blocks automatic loading, the form says so and offers **Upload image** right under the message (for a new wish, save it first and upload from its edit panel); a page that is too large is reported as too large. To read the first link again, press **Reload from first link**.
**Price** and **Currency**: a rough price helps others plan.
**Priority**: **Top wish**, **Would love** or **Nice to have**.
**Notes**: size, colour, or anything else.
**Image**: upload a JPEG, PNG or WebP picture of up to 5 MB, or press **Load image from link** to take one from the shop page.

blocks.text: When you get a gift, open the wish and choose **Mark as received** and confirm. Received wishes move out of the way. Press **Show received** to see them again. If you marked a wish by mistake, open it in the Received section, choose **Move back to my list** and confirm: the wish is active and editable again.

sections.title: Sharing a product from your phone

blocks.title: Where to tap
items: Open the product page in your phone's browser.
Use the browser's **Share** command and choose **FamilyHUB**.
The new wish form opens on your own list with the link and the title already filled in, and the picture is looked up as when you paste a link.
Check it and press **Save wish**.
Nothing is saved until you press **Save wish**. Close the form to throw the shared link away.

It works on Android with Chrome, after FamilyHUB has been installed on the home screen. If FamilyHUB is missing from the Share list, remove the app and install it again once, because the Share entry is added when the app is installed.
iPhone and iPad (Safari) cannot share to installed web apps. There, copy the link, open **Add wish** and paste it into **Links**.
Group lists are not a share target: the wish always goes to your own list. You can move on from there as usual.

sections.title: Reserving a gift and buying together

blocks.text: On somebody else's list, open a wish to see the **Reservation** box.

blocks.title: Where to click
items: Press **Reserve gift**. Now everyone but the owner sees that you are buying it.
Changed your mind? Press **Cancel reservation**.
Want to share the cost? Press **Open for co-buying**. Other people can then press **Join co-buy** and, if they like, type their share.
Press **Close co-buying** when the group is complete. Anyone who joined can press **Leave co-buy**.

blocks.text: The list **Your shopping** shows the gifts you reserved and how much you promised to pay. Gifts you reserved on a group list appear there under the name of that list.
If two people try to reserve the same gift at the same moment, the first one wins and the other sees a short message. Nothing breaks.

A group list is one list for several people, for example a couple who want to collect things together. Group lists appear in the **Group lists** row under the person buttons. Anyone with Edit on the Wishlist can create one. Only family members who can sign in and have Edit on the Wishlist can be members.

blocks.title: Creating a group list
items: Press **New group list**.
Type a name (up to 80 characters).
Choose the mode: **Gifts from others** or **Shared purchases**.
Tick the members. You are always a member.
Press **Create list**.

blocks.text: Members are added directly. Nobody has to accept. The two modes work like this:

items: **Gifts from others**: the group is the one receiving gifts. The rest of the family reserves and buys for the list, and nobody in the group sees what is reserved or by whom, exactly like your own list.
**Shared purchases**: only the group sees the list. Everyone in it sees who reserved or bought what, and the members can reserve and buy together.

blocks.text: Every member can add, edit and remove wishes. Wishes marked as received show who marked them. Open the list and press **Manage list** to rename it, change the members or change the mode. Every member can do this.

items: **Changing the mode**: you are asked to confirm, because all reservations on the list are cancelled and nobody is told what was reserved.
**Leave this list**: you no longer see the list. If it is a Shared purchases list, your reservations on it are cancelled. The last member cannot leave and must delete the list instead.
**Delete list**: the list, all its wishes and their pictures are deleted, and the reservations on it are cancelled. This cannot be undone.
**Limits**: up to 12 members on a list and up to 10 group lists per person.

blocks.text: Someone who is removed from a Gifts from others list, or leaves it, becomes an ordinary giver and can then see its reservations, like a removed wishlist manager. Someone who is added to a Gifts from others list loses their own reservations on it, so that nothing is revealed to them.
Group lists have no occasions of their own. Birthdays and name days stay personal.

sections.title: Why you never see who reserved your own wishes

blocks.text: This is on purpose, so gifts stay a surprise. On your own list you cannot see whether a wish is reserved, who reserved it, or who is co-buying. Everyone else can. The same applies to the members of a Gifts from others group list (see [Group lists](#group-lists)). The app also never sends you reminders about your own birthday or name day.
The **Occasions** page lists upcoming birthdays, name days, Christmas and your own occasions. The Overview also shows the next ones in the coming 60 days.

items: **Dates by member**: for each person you can set a birth date and a name day. Choose **Edit dates**, pick the name day calendar (**Slovak calendar**, **Polish calendar** or none), search for a name, and pick the day.
**Custom occasions**: press **Add occasion**, type a title and date, choose **Repeat every year** if you like, and say whether it is for one person or the **Whole family**.

blocks.text: To get a reminder before an occasion, use [Settings > Notifications](/settings/notifications) and choose 14, 7, 3 or 1 day before.
A child, or anyone who finds it hard to keep a list, can have a manager. The administrator chooses the managers (see [Wishlist managers](admin#wishlist-managers)).

If you are a manager, the child's button is in your row and a banner says **You are managing** the list. You can add and edit wishes, and you see the list exactly as the child does: with no reservations. That keeps the surprise for the child too.
A child added by the administrator has a list like any other member. It appears among the people at the top of the Wishlist for everyone who can see the Wishlist.
The parents chosen when the child was added are its managers. They add and edit wishes on the child's list and see it the way the child does (see [Wishlist managers](admin#wishlist-managers)).

blocks.title: Changing the child's name or photo
items: Open the account menu and choose [Profile settings](/profile).
Under **People you manage**, press **Edit** next to the child.
Change the name or the photo.

blocks.text: An administrator can do the same under Members and access. Nobody else can change a child's name or photo.
